title: Survival of mouse oocytes after being cooled in a vitrification solution to −196°C at 95° to 70,000°C/min and warmed at 610° to 118,000°C/min: A new paradigm for cryopreservation by vitrification

cell_and_endpoint.model: Mature unfertilized metaphase-II oocytes from female ICR mice
cell_and_endpoint.media: EAFS 10/10 in PB1: 10% v/v ethylene glycol, 10.7% w/v acetamide, final 0.4 M sucrose and 24% w/v Ficoll 70
cell_and_endpoint.handling: 0.1 μl EAFS containing about 6 oocytes on a Cryotop; 20 cooling/warming combinations, generally 4–6 replicate runs each
cell_and_endpoint.endpoint: Binary viability based on osmotic responsiveness and morphology during sucrose/PB1 exposure, after PB1 transfer, and after 2 h in modified M16

arms.warming_media: 2 ml of 0.5 M sucrose/PB1 at 0°C or 23°C, or room-temperature air, with Cryotop insulation varied
arms.storage: Cryotops cooled to −196°C in liquid nitrogen; vitrification with concentrated glass-forming solutes, distinct from slow equilibrium freezing

results: The highest warming rate produced approximately 70–85% survival across cooling rates; the lowest warming rate produced approximately 25–0% survival as cooling rate increased. The paper discusses intracellular ice growth by recrystallization and presents devitrification as an alternative possibility.
exact_supporting_quotes: The ability to manifest these characteristics after two hours in M16 is considered a rather stringent test of viability.
limitations: Mouse oocytes and a vitrification solution; transfer to iPSC systems is not established.
Survival is a morphology/osmotic-response endpoint after 2 h culture, not long-term developmental function.
The mechanistic explanation includes an alternative possibility and is not direct intracellular ice imaging.
review_note: Full-text methods and results reviewed for extraction planning; root agent retains final extraction decisions.
